title: Oral Wegovy super-responders are characterized by greater pretreatment weight gain, faster early dose escalation, and larger on-treatment blood pressure reductions
content:
Abstract
Early weight-loss responses to oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) vary substantially, and super-responders are incompletely characterized. Using de-identified electronic health records, we studied 9287 GLP-1 RA-naive patients prescribed oral Wegovy. Of 8381 patients with an index weight, 3011 had a weight between 30 and 180 days and were classified by their best percent weight change as non-responders (no loss), responders (>0%–5% loss), strong responders (>5%–10%), or super-responders (>10%). Body weight was traced back 5 years, and HbA1c, blood pressure, comorbidities, dose escalation, and phenotypes extracted from clinical notes using Artificial Intelligence (AI)-augmented curation were compared across these treatment response groups. Super-responders weighed less at initiation than non-responders (94.1 vs. 101.7 kg; P < .001) and had weighed 7.6% less 5 years earlier, against 0.8% less among non-responders (P < .001). Among patients of the same starting weight, faster weight gain between 5 years and 6 months before treatment predicted lower weight at day 90 (0.11 kg per year; P = .015). Super-responders lost 7.2% by day 60 and 11.4% by day 90, returning within 2 months to their weight from 5 years earlier. Baseline Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and blood pressure did not differ across groups, and the share of women and of type 2 diabetes varied only modestly with response. Super-responders escalated earlier (37% vs. 24% were prescribed >1.5 mg at day 30; P = .001) and their systolic blood pressure fell more by day 90 (10.2 vs. 3.3 mmHg; P = .006). Among 1978 phenotypes AI-curated from unstructured clinical notes, before the first prescription, severe obesity was documented less in super-responders (19.4% vs. 36.1%; P < .001; q = 0.003). Pre-treatment weight trajectory and dosage emerged as associates of early response, but the outcome-defined groups and short follow-up make these findings hypothesis-generating.
